subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted API vs current provider)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Richardson <sam@finlytics.com>, Priya Nair <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T15:12:00Z
Subject: Recap + next steps — p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted API vs current provider)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on performance qualification: 

Summary of what we heard from you on the call:
- Current provider: end-to-end p95 observed ~220ms, p99 ~680ms (measurements include app network + provider processing).
- Peak concurrency: ~300 concurrent inference sessions during batch windows; sustained baseline ~80–120 concurrent.
- Typical payloads: ~350 token inputs, ~150 token outputs for recommendation flows; some shorter (<64 tokens) low-latency paths for search rerank.
- Streaming: you need token-streaming support for the conversational assistant (progressive output for UI).
- Throughput target for steady-state: ~1k reqs/min with short spikes to ~2k reqs/min for flash events.

Redwood initial assessment (high level):
- Hosted API is capable of p95 in the 120–180ms range for 512-token-equivalent end-to-end in many configs; p99 will be higher (typically 350–450ms) depending on network routing and cold-starts.
- Key variables: batching policy, request size distribution, KV-cache effectiveness for streaming scenarios, and where your p99 tail is dominated by network vs inference.

Proposed next steps (recommended):
1) Share representative traces and a small sample of request/response sizes (you mentioned attaching 24 hours of p95/p99 logs).
2) Redwood runs a 2-week PoC: we mirror your traffic profile in our test harness, measure end-to-end p95/p99 for both Hosted API and a tuned Dedicated config, and produce an SLO matrix.
3) Define success criteria up front: e.g., p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 600ms for 95% of test windows, with streaming behavior validated in the UI.
4) Canary plan: start with non-critical traffic for 72 hours then ramp to 100% if targets are met.

I attached a short SLO matrix template (redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx) to capture payload distributions and desired SLOs — can you fill the shaded fields (typical tok in/out, peak conc, SLA importance) and send back? Also please attach the provider logs you referenced.

I’ll loop in Aditya and Ben on the technical plan — they’ll propose the exact test harness and measurement scripts.

If this all looks good I’ll send an updated statement of work for the PoC.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)

From: Sam Richardson <sam@finlytics.com>

Date: 2026-07-13T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted API vs current provider)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That plan sounds good. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The p95/p99 numbers I quoted were measured from our app servers to the provider (so they include our edge + provider processing). We can provide raw tcpdump-level logs or the aggregated percentiles — which is more helpful for you?
- Streaming is required for the assistant UI; we need <150ms first token latency for a good UX on short responses (<64 tokens). That said, the longer responses can tolerate higher p95 if streaming starts early.
- For payloads: the 350/150 token figure is the heavy path; about 60% of requests are under 128 tokens.

We’ll share 48–72 hours of percentile logs and a sample of request traces (zipped) by tomorrow afternoon. We can also provide a short internal test harness that emits representative traffic if that helps.

Assume go for the 2-week PoC — please send the SOW and we’ll route to procurement.

Best,
Sam
CTO — FinLytics
sam@finlytics.com

Attachments referenced: finlytics-current-provider-logs.zip (zipped log export, ~6MB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — technical plan notes

Quick notes on the PoC setup and what we need from FinLytics: 
- We should capture both cold-start and steady-state tails. Ask them to include timestamps for any retry/backoff events in their logs so we can attribute tail spikes correctly.
- Streaming first-token latency: we can instrument chunked transfer and measure TTF (time-to-first-token) separately from full-response p95/p99. For UX success we should guarantee TTF < 150ms on short responses as Sam requested.
- Concurrency shaping: replicate their peak concurrency profile (300 simultaneous) and also a burst curve to 2k rps-ish (sustained minute-level).
- Measurement: synthetic generator + real sample traces. We’ll run both hosted (multi-tenant) and dedicated nodes; important to test with their payload distribution to avoid optimistic batching.
- Logs: request/response sizes, client RTT (if available), and per-request token counts. If they can include typical client location (US east/west) that helps with routing sims.

Action items for us:
- I’ll prepare the harness config and upload to the internal PoC link.
- Ben: can you prepare an estimated cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for the expected peak traffic? Put it in the SLO matrix tab.

—Aditya
Senior Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Related internal link: https://redwood-internal.test/poctest-harness/FINLY-2026

Subject: Next steps: PoC SOW and success criteria

Thanks Sam / Priya —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the logs. Next steps from Redwood: 
1) I attached a filled SLO matrix template with our preliminary targets based on your payloads. Please review the shaded fields and confirm token counts / peak concurrency.
2) Redwood will provision a PoC: 2 weeks, mirror traffic profile, measure TTF (time-to-first-token), end-to-end p95/p99, and streaming behavior.
3) Success criteria proposed (we can adjust):
   - p95 (end-to-end) <= 200ms for 95% of test windows
   - p99 (end-to-end) <= 600ms
   - TTF (first token) < 150ms for responses <64 tokens in 95% of short-response requests
   - No functional regressions in output quality (we’ll run a small eval set from your prompts)
4) Canary plan: 72 hours at 20% production traffic, then ramp over 48 hours if targets met.

Procurement / SOW: I’ll send a short SOW and PoC agreement by end of day tomorrow. Ben will include an estimated cost comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated for the expected peak profile.

If you’re good with that I’ll kick off the internal provisioning and send the PoC access + test harness configs.

Best,
Marissa
